headline: High risk of prompt injection and cascading errors: LangGraph can pass untrusted graph outputs into PaddleOCR-driven document workflows without built-in isolation or verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LangGraph can ingest and route outputs between nodes, and its self-isolation is none; PaddleOCR processes documents/images that may contain attacker-controlled text. The pair has a plausible shared-file or pipeline bridge, but no documented direct channel or parser permissiveness is shown, so I rate this as medium rather than high.
conditions: IF LangGraph nodes read PaddleOCR output files or markdown as instructions without sanitization
IF a shared workspace or queue carries OCR text into agent prompts
mitigations: Add a strict content-to-instructions separator in the orchestrator
Require allowlisted prompt templates for any OCR-derived text
Insert a 1-minute manual review step before tool execution
Log and reject any OCR text containing role/instruction markers
requires-engineering: add provenance tags from OCR output to downstream prompts

B_data_leakage.rationale: LangGraph explicitly handles model provider API keys and application-defined graph state, while PaddleOCR touches documents and images. If they share a workspace or graph state, sensitive document contents can flow into LangGraph outputs or external model calls. The profiles do not prove default sharing, so medium is the highest justified severity.
conditions: IF both agents access the same document workspace or checkpointer state
IF LangGraph forwards OCR text to third-party model providers
mitigations: Separate document storage from orchestration state
Redact secrets before any LangGraph model call
Restrict PaddleOCR inputs to non-sensitive documents
Review outbound prompts for embedded file contents
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on shared state

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LangGraph has broad filesystem write and shell execution, plus shared checkpointer state across instances; PaddleOCR has allowlisted network egress and browser capability. Even without explicit write access in PaddleOCR, overlapping mutable resources via shared files or orchestration state can create conflicts. Uncertainty about PaddleOCR write paths escalates to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace or checkpoint-backed state
IF PaddleOCR browser/network actions mutate shared artifacts
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent
Disable concurrent writes to shared checkpoints
Serialize access to any shared document store
Use file locks around generated artifacts
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph can produce intermediate facts or transformed text, and PaddleOCR is a document-processing agent that may consume those outputs. If PaddleOCR treats LangGraph output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream document extraction or translation. No verification step is documented, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR consumes LangGraph-generated text without independent validation
IF LangGraph output is used as the sole source for document parsing or translation
mitigations: Require a verification pass before acting on LangGraph output
Compare OCR results against source documents
Flag low-confidence extractions for manual review
Keep raw source documents alongside transformed outputs
requires-engineering: add confidence propagation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not declare conflicting residency, certification, or retention policies. LangGraph handles model-provider API keys and graph state, while PaddleOCR touches documents and images, but the profiles do not show a concrete compliance mismatch. I cite both because the risk is about their combined data handling, though no breach is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated documents are routed through a deployment with undocumented retention
IF one agent logs document contents longer than the other
mitigations: Document retention settings for both agents
Avoid regulated data in shared test runs
Review logging for document contents
Publish a short data-flow map
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies
